touches.text: Messages sit in a SMALL buffer in memory. WHY: in memory is faster.

A message nobody picks up within n milliseconds is pushed out of the buffer to the database, into a table that is just a table of messages. That table is the bus's exception to the memory model (4.3.1.5): it is not learning, and the buffer in front of it is what keeps the bus fast.

Who holds tables: every table of learning is a tree in the memory model (4.3.1.5), owned by the librarian and delegated to the devices that learn. A table that is not learning is an exception and names why; the bus's message table is the first (5.5.3.4.1).
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
